newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian mill workers disrupt deliveries.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian mill workers disrupt deliveries.

text.p: More than 1,000 workers with Central Egypt Flour Mills disrupted deliveries of flour to customers on Thursday in protest at a decision to stop supplying them with a monthly flour allowance.
Work continued inside the mills but the workers closed the gates and stopped bakery owners picking up supplies.
A local official later persuaded them to resume normal work by promising that the governor of Assiut province would do his best to overturn the decision.
The protest was by 1,360 workers at the company's seven mills and 14 warehouses in Assiut province south of Cairo, said trade union leader Mohamed el-Berri.
The company, which has been partially privatised this year, also operates in neighbouring provinces.
Under arrangements in place for the last 10 years, the workers receive 100 kg (220 lb) of flour a month and the company deducts the retail value of the flour from their wages.
The workers argued that it was more convenient to obtain their flour in this way, rather than buying it from the shops.
